submission.justification: Recommend Absorber-F2 with 5.4 mm plates. Absorber-F2 is one of the listed candidate absorber materials and consistently gives the best 100 GeV electron energy resolution in the Geant4 scans. A coarse scan showed F2 outperforming F3 and F1 at all comparable thicknesses near their optima; the best coarse alternatives were about 3.85% for F3 and 5.07% for F1, while F2 was about 3.1–3.2% near 5–6 mm. A finer replicated scan of F2 around the minimum found the lowest mean resolution near 5.4 mm, approximately 3.12% at 100 GeV, with nearby points generally higher. The mechanical support, cooling, and readout documents indicate no absorber-specific incompatibility for the candidates, so choosing F2 does not introduce a documented maintenance/service-access limitation.

requirements.requirement: Goal: Achieve the best possible energy resolution at 100 GeV.
requirements.evidence: Simulation scan selected the lowest-resolution option found: Absorber-F2 at 5.4 mm. Replicated runs at 5.4 mm averaged about 3.12% at 100 GeV; F3's best sampled region was about 3.85% and F1's was about 5.07%.

requirements.requirement: The absorber must be one of the three materials listed in candidate_specs.md.
requirements.evidence: candidate_specs.md lists Absorber-F1, Absorber-F2, and Absorber-F3; the recommendation uses Absorber-F2.

requirements.requirement: The calorimeter must allow hands-on maintenance during shutdowns.
requirements.evidence: Project documents report that the mechanical support design is compatible with every candidate absorber; cooling heat load is dominated by front-end electronics; and the readout/ASIC are common to all absorber options. No document flags Absorber-F2 as incompatible with shutdown maintenance access.
The recommended plate thickness is 5.4 mm, within the allowed 2–10 mm range.

requirements.requirement: Finish by submitting one recommended material and plate thickness.
requirements.evidence: Submitted one recommendation: Absorber-F2 with 5.4 mm plates.
